name: veterinary_clinic_system_019_run_status_audit
instruction:
Run the boarding occupancy-board audit as of the episode date. The occupancy board and reservation book must agree.

For every boarding_runs record:
- If there is a checked_in reservation assigned to that run (run_id matches and reservation status = 'checked_in'), the run must be status='occupied' and current_patient_id must equal that reservation's patient_id.
- If there is no checked_in reservation on that run, the run must be 'available' unless its status is already 'maintenance' or 'cleaning' (leave those as-is).

For every run that is not consistent with the rule above, repair the run side only: set the correct status and current_patient_id, and push an audit_log entry with action='RUN_STATUS_REPAIR', actor='system', actor_role='front_desk', target_collection='boarding_runs', target_id=<run_id>, details='Run <run_number> repaired to <status> for batch <batch_code>', occurred_at=<episode_date with time>, batch_code.

Regardless of whether a run was repaired, set `audited` = the live batch_code on every run.

A 'run_conflict' is a reserved reservation whose stay overlaps the episode date (check_in <= episode_date <= check_out) and whose run is currently occupied by a different checked_in reservation. Count these in the report but do not modify any reservation.

Finally, create exactly one ops_reports row 'boarding_run_audit' keyed by batch_code with: episode_date, audited_run_count (must equal the total number of boarding_runs), conflict_count, run_status_summary (dict {location_name: {available, occupied, maintenance, cleaning}}), and repaired_run_count. Overwrite any existing row for this batch.

Do not touch any reservation.
_max_steps_note: Measured against a live container in the QC session; placeholder because this codegen-only session cannot run gold.
_par_steps_note: Measured against a live container in the QC session; placeholder because this codegen-only session cannot run gold.

success_criteria.summary: Every run has audited=batch_code. Each run's status and current_patient_id match the live checked_in reservation state: 'occupied' + reservation.patient_id where a checked_in reservation exists, otherwise 'available' unless 'maintenance'/'cleaning'. Any repaired run has an audit_log entry. The ops_reports 'boarding_run_audit' row contains the correct audited_run_count (= total runs), conflict_count (reserved overlapping an occupied run), run_status_summary, and repaired_run_count. All aggregates are recomputed via raw-row Python and independent SQL. No reservations are modified.

checks.expect: Every run has audited=batch and correct status/current_patient_id; only status, current_patient_id, and audited may change
One RUN_STATUS_REPAIR entry per repaired run, no extras
Exactly one boarding_run_audit row per batch with correct counts and summary
conflict_count and run_status_summary agree between raw-row Python and independent SQL JOIN/GROUP BY

hazards: All runs are already consistent with checked_in reservations in the snapshot: runs 1-5 are 'occupied' with current_patient_id matching reservations 1-5 (patients 2, 4, 6, 8, 10), and runs 6-17 are 'available'. A solution that 'repairs' runs based on the most recent reservation (including reserved) will set run 3 to patient 77 (reservation 99) or run 4 to patient 73 (reservation 98) and fail.
The `audited` field must be set on all 17 runs, not just the ones that changed. A solution that only touches inconsistent runs leaves the other 12 runs un-audited.

Run conflicts at default episode 2026-09-30: reserved reservations 98 (run 4, occupied by reservation 4) and 99 (run 3, occupied by reservation 3) overlap the episode. These are the only two conflicts; other active reserved reservations are on available runs.
Reserved reservations that are past their check_out (e.g., id 8 check_out 2026-09-28 at default ep) must not be counted as conflicts because they do not overlap the episode.
Runs with status 'maintenance' or 'cleaning' and no checked_in reservation must be left as-is. The seed has none, but a verifier will test this branch on reseed.
Idempotency: a second run must set the same audited value and leave the same final state, and must not duplicate the ops_reports or audit_log rows.

The v2 task audits all runs, sets audited on all of them, reports conflicts without modifying reservations, and uses dual-path verification.
